evidence.excerpt: Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.
